findingCopy.applyWhen: Apply this when you notice your feet shifting or when you feel tempted to step out of the stance between repetitions.
findingCopy.correction: Keep your feet planted in the initial split stance throughout the entire set instead of stepping out or walking forward between reps.
findingCopy.successCheck: The feet remain in their original positions on the floor from the first repetition to the last.
findingCopy.whyItMatters: Keeping the feet in a fixed position ensures the stance width and length remain identical for every repetition, making the movement path more repeatable.

findingCopy.cue: Reach the same visible endpoints while keeping the support position consistent.
findingCopy.title: Consistent Depth Across Repetitions
findingCopy.detail: The depth of the split squat is highly consistent across all repetitions, with the back knee consistently approaching the floor to a similar height.
findingCopy.whyItMatters: Reaching a consistent bottom endpoint ensures that each repetition covers the same range of motion, making your overall performance easier to replicate.

findingCopy.cue: Change direction smoothly without bouncing or dropping the load.
findingCopy.title: Controlled Tempo and Smooth Transitions
findingCopy.detail: The movement is performed with a controlled tempo during both the descent and ascent phases, with a smooth transition at the bottom of each repetition.
findingCopy.whyItMatters: A controlled descent and smooth transition prevent momentum from altering your movement path, leading to a highly repeatable technique.

nextSetPlan.action: Focus on keeping your feet glued to their starting positions on the floor between repetitions 3 and 4.
nextSetPlan.rationale: Addressing the step-out observed between these reps will help maintain a consistent stance length and width for the entire set.
nextSetPlan.successCheck: Your feet do not move or step forward at any point during the set.
